summary: Since small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl landed, master runs no side stream at T<=32, so this change only affects verify_16 (T=128) and verify_32 (T=256). There it is a plausible, low-risk overlap worth about 1-2% per shape, but only about +0.4% on the headline, so judge it on those four shapes' times and not on the headline.
justification: The mechanism holds at T>32 only. On master (f1f2f35c), kernel_fn takes the dense-chain path (_dl_forward, no side stream) whenever tokens <= DL_MAX_TOKENS=32, and the BEST profile shows dl_pooler_router_kernel at decode_1/16/32 and verify_1, so that path was ON. That makes all four T<=32 'faster' expectations (decode_1/16/32, verify_1) wrong: those shapes run code this change does not touch and should read flat. The hypothesis was written while the dense chain was still being judged and admits the overlap. At T=128/256 the master non-dl branch runs, in order: pooler GEMM (~25-28 us, nvjet 64x64 / 128x128) on main in parallel with the router hi+lo mm, the add and routing on the side stream; then the join; then pre_expert_norm (~6 us), the sub/mod, the expert_map gather, the fp32 cast and moe_align_block_size (~8-10 us at T=128 by the hypothesis's own estimate), all serial. Moving the dispatch before the join and the pre-norm before the join changes the critical path from ~max(pooler, router) + norm + dispatch to max(pooler + norm, router + routing + dispatch). The saving is roughly min(norm, dispatch) plus slack, about 6-10 us of 448/599 us (verify_16) and 627/911 us (verify_32): +1-2% on sliding and less on full. The per-shape median err is 4-5 us, so a ~8 us move is only marginally resolvable per shape, a bit better across the two loads (46+16 weights). It is invisible in the headline geomean: about +0.4% against a CI of about +/-1.5%. Weakest link: the 'side ~33 us vs main ~31 us' budget at T=128, and worse at T=256. The router hi+lo mm, routing and align all grow with T, while pooler + norm is weight-bound and nearly flat. At verify_32 the side branch is likely the critical path after the change, so the saving drops to whatever dispatch time still hides behind the pooler. On top of that, the small side kernels compete with a full-SM pooler GEMM for SMs, so 'overlap' can turn into queueing (the same unverified contention suspect named for bf16-shape-gated-triton-gemms-small-t). The profile top-4 does not list align/gather/routing at T=128/256, so the ~10 us align figure is unverified.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (base): at T<=32 the change is a no-op because there is no side stream. Decode_1/16/32 and verify_1 deltas are pure noise and must not be credited. If the run's DL log line says 'PATH CHOSEN = MASTER at every T' (self-check or compile fallback), the change also covers T<=32 and the decode expectations apply. The judge must read that line before attributing anything.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: it sets the side-branch length at T>1 (two bf16 mm, hi and lo, plus the add, ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS=1). The saving is capped by how much the side branch exceeds pooler + norm, so a loss or a flat result at verify_32 could reflect the hi+lo router being long rather than the dispatch move itself.

marlin-block-m-cap-16: it fixes block_size_m=16 at T=128/256, which sets moe_align_block_size's padded output size and its cost. With the old 48/64 the align would be cheaper and the overlap saving smaller. This is a minor magnitude effect only, not a sign flip.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-t and fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: neither confounds. The first is T<32 only and the second only touches attention before the fork.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change keeps the same kernel set, arguments and dtypes and only moves stream placement and order, so a verify_16/32 gain can only come from the overlap, and a loss can only come from side-stream SM contention or the side branch becoming the critical path. A control that splits the two sub-moves (pre-norm before the join vs dispatch on the side stream) would chase a ~3-5 us difference below the 4-5 us per-shape err, so it could not be read. An ab-revert of the hilo router would change the numerics path and is not meaningful. For attribution: read verify_16/verify_32 per-shape medians against BEST job 81ee6714b7614a99 (sliding 447.6/626.8 us, full 599.4/910.9 us), check that GPU busy rose or stayed flat while the kernel rows stayed unchanged, and confirm the DL line says PATH CHOSEN = DENSE-CHAIN at T <= 32. Treat decode/verify_1 as controls that should be flat. moe-chain-cuda-swapab-expert-once-large-t FAILED, so master's align at T>32 stays and this hypothesis stands on its own: it does not depend on that parent winning.
rules_flags: None blocking. No host sync: moe_align_block_size and the gather are device-only, and _block_size_m reads only the shape. Nothing is cached from data. Precision is unchanged.

Implementation hazard, not a rule: keep master's dense-chain call _experts(..., align=align) working, either by keeping _experts as a thin wrapper or by having the dl path build the same dispatch tuple for _expert_compute. Do not route T<=32 through the new side-stream code.

Allocations moved onto the side stream (local_ids, fp32 topk_weights, sorted_ids, block_experts, n_padded, plus align's internal buffers) need record_stream(main_stream) outside capture, as the hypothesis says. Inside capture, the graph pool covers them. Missing even one would be a silent use-after-free outside graphs (the correctness check runs eagerly).
open_questions: Does moe_align_block_size at T=128/256 with block 16 actually take ~8-10 us? It is not in the profile top-4. Its real cost bounds the gain.
At T=256, does router hi+lo + routing + dispatch exceed pooler + pre-norm? If so, the verify_32 gain collapses to near zero.
Does the nvjet pooler GEMM occupy all 132 SMs for its whole duration, so that side-stream kernels serialize anyway? A GPU-busy and overlap read from the profile would settle it.
